title: The ¥1.06m social-insurance wall is set to disappear in October
summary: FACT: Japan has enacted removal of the ¥88,000 monthly wage test behind the so-called ¥1.06 million social-insurance wall, and MHLW currently says the change is planned for October 2026. For many part-time workers at covered employers, the practical line to watch becomes the contracted 20-hours-per-week threshold rather than a ¥1.06 million annual-income target.
why_it_matters: Kung part-time ka at ina-adjust mo ang oras para manatili sa ilalim ng ¥88,000 monthly test, that rule is about to stop being the key test. But the ¥1.30 million dependent-family threshold is a separate rule and does not disappear with this change.

claims.text: The 2025 pension reform law provides for abolition of the ¥88,000 monthly wage requirement, and MHLW currently says abolition is planned for October 2026.

Under the current short-time-worker rules, covered workers generally need at least 20 scheduled hours per week, monthly scheduled wages of at least ¥88,000, non-student status, and employment at a covered establishment; employment expected to exceed two months is also required.

The current company-size test is more than 50 covered employees; it is scheduled to shrink to more than 35 employees in October 2027, more than 20 in October 2029, more than 10 in October 2032, and disappear in October 2035.
The separate ¥1.30 million dependent-family social-insurance threshold remains a different rule; removal of the ¥1.06 million wage test does not abolish it.
claims.basis: MHLW distinguishes the ¥1.06 million employee-insurance threshold from the ¥1.30 million dependent threshold.

claims.text: MHLW states that joining employee social insurance can reduce take-home pay because premiums arise, while also adding Employees' Pension coverage and benefits such as sickness allowance and maternity allowance.
By September 3, 2026, all prefectural minimum-wage councils had submitted 2026 revision figures, with a national weighted-average proposed minimum wage of ¥1,177.

For workers who have been managing schedules around the ¥88,000 wage test, checking contracted weekly hours and employer coverage before October is more useful than relying on a ¥1.06 million annual-income target.
claims.basis: Removing the wage requirement leaves working-hours and establishment coverage as the key short-time-worker tests.

content.policy_status: ENACTED, NOT YET EFFECTIVE. The 2025 pension reform law authorizes abolition of the wage requirement. As of September 6, 2026, MHLW's public guidance says implementation is planned for October 2026; ALAM is not treating October 1 as final until an official implementation date is explicitly confirmed.
content.key_message: Kung part-time ka, stop treating ¥1.06M as the only number to manage. Check your contracted weekly hours and whether your employer is a covered workplace before October.
content.who_is_affected: Primarily part-time and other short-time workers who are below three-quarters of normal full-time hours and work at employers covered by the short-time-worker rules. The immediate 2026 company-size rule is generally establishments with more than 50 covered employees; smaller employers expand later under the statutory schedule.
content.when: MHLW currently says the ¥88,000 monthly wage requirement is planned to be abolished in October 2026. The ministry pages reviewed by ALAM still describe the date as planned, so confirm the final effective date before making payroll or work-hour decisions.
content.financial_impact: VARIABLE. Newly joining employee social insurance can lower monthly take-home pay because health-insurance and pension premiums begin, but it also adds employer-paid contributions and stronger pension/leave-income protection. ALAM is not publishing a generic yen loss because the actual premium depends on pay, age, prefecture/insurer and household situation.
content.risk_if_ignored: MEDIUM to HIGH for households deliberately controlling part-time hours or wages to preserve dependent status or avoid employee-insurance enrollment. The common mistake is assuming every 'income wall' disappears at once.
content.deadline: Before your employer's first payroll/scheduling cycle affected by the October 2026 change; verify the final effective date in official MHLW/Japan Pension Service guidance.
content.effort: LOW. The first check is your employment contract, scheduled weekly hours and employer coverage status.
content.potential_benefit: Avoid a surprise social-insurance deduction or unnecessary work-hour restriction caused by relying on an outdated ¥1.06 million rule of thumb.
content.downside: Do not cut hours automatically. Employee social insurance also provides added pension rights and income-protection benefits, and the separate ¥1.30 million dependent threshold may still matter depending on your case.
content.what_would_change_mind: ALAM would update this if the government changes the October timing, delays implementation, modifies remaining eligibility conditions, or changes the dependent-family threshold.

30 sec: What happened: Japan has enacted removal of the ¥88,000 monthly wage test behind the '¥1.06 million wall'; MHLW says October 2026 is the planned timing.
Why it matters: For covered part-time workers, the practical boundary shifts toward contracted weekly hours, especially the 20-hour test.
What to do: Check your contract, weekly hours and employer coverage before October payroll/scheduling.
Bottom line: The ¥1.06M wall is changing, but the separate ¥1.30M dependent threshold does not vanish with it.
reading_levels.2 min: Today, the familiar '¥1.06 million wall' is really a monthly scheduled-wage test of ¥88,000 used together with weekly-hours, student-status and employer-size conditions. The 2025 pension reform removes that wage test, and MHLW currently says the change is planned for October 2026. That does not mean every part-timer suddenly enters social insurance, nor does it erase the separate ¥1.30 million dependent-family rule. For many workers, the more important question becomes whether the employment contract is for at least 20 hours per week and whether the workplace is covered.

outcomes: Explain what the '¥1.06 million wall' actually is.
Know which eligibility test is being removed and which ones remain.
Distinguish the ¥1.06 million employee-insurance rule from the separate ¥1.30 million dependent rule.
Know what to check with HR before October.
learning.background: The '¥1.06 million wall' is shorthand, not a literal annual-income test. Under today's short-time-worker system, one key condition is scheduled monthly wages of at least ¥88,000; ¥88,000 times 12 is roughly ¥1.06 million. Japan's 2025 pension reform removes that wage condition as minimum wages rise, while expanding employee social-insurance coverage over time.

terms.term: 所定労働時間 (scheduled working hours)
terms.meaning: The regular hours written or established for your job, rather than occasional overtime.
terms.why_it_matters: The 20-hours-per-week test remains central after the wage test is removed.

terms.term: 被扶養者 (dependent under health insurance)
terms.meaning: A family member covered under another insured person's health-insurance plan when the dependency rules are met.
terms.why_it_matters: The separate ¥1.30 million income threshold belongs to this dependency system and is not the same as the ¥1.06 million wage test.

how_it_works.title: Today: several tests operate together
how_it_works.explanation: For short-time workers at covered establishments, current rules look at weekly scheduled hours, monthly scheduled wages, student status and other eligibility conditions.

how_it_works.title: October: the ¥88,000 wage test is scheduled to go
how_it_works.explanation: MHLW says the wage requirement is planned for abolition in October 2026 because legal minimum wages have risen enough that someone working 20 hours a week at the minimum wage generally clears that amount anyway.

how_it_works.title: The 20-hour line remains
how_it_works.explanation: Removing the wage test does not remove the scheduled-hours test, so employment contracts and recurring schedules become more important for workers managing social-insurance eligibility.

how_it_works.title: The ¥1.30 million rule is separate
how_it_works.explanation: The dependent-family threshold applies to a different part of the social-insurance system. Do not assume that news about the ¥1.06 million wall means all dependency rules disappear.

learning.example: Example: a worker at a covered employer who schedules 20 hours every week should not assume staying below ¥88,000 in scheduled monthly wages will continue to keep them outside employee social insurance after the wage test is abolished. Their exact eligibility still depends on the remaining official conditions.
takeaways: ¥1.06 million is shorthand for the current ¥88,000 monthly scheduled-wage test.
That wage test is planned for abolition in October 2026.
The separate ¥1.30 million dependent threshold does not disappear with this change.
Check the final effective date and your own contract/HR classification before changing hours.

action_plan.goal: Know whether the October social-insurance change is likely to affect your household before work schedules or payroll deductions change.
action_plan.who_should_act: Part-time/short-time workers and households that deliberately manage work hours or income around social-insurance dependency. Full-time workers already enrolled in employee social insurance generally do not need to act because of this specific rule change.
action_plan.deadline: Before the first October 2026 scheduling/payroll cycle that your employer says is affected, after confirming the final government effective date.
prepare: Employment contract or written work conditions
Employer or HR information on whether the workplace is a covered establishment
If relevant, current dependent-family insurance status

steps.action: Read your employment contract or written work conditions and identify the regular weekly hours.
steps.how: Use contracted/scheduled hours, not a single busy week's overtime.
steps.done_when: You know whether your scheduled hours are below, at, or above 20 hours per week.

steps.step: Confirm whether your workplace is covered
steps.action: Ask HR/payroll whether the workplace is a current 特定適用事業所 or otherwise subject to short-time-worker employee-insurance coverage.
steps.how: Use the employer's formal social-insurance classification, not just the total headcount you can see at your branch.
steps.done_when: HR confirms whether the short-time-worker rules apply to your workplace.

steps.action: Ask HR whether your employee-insurance status or payroll deduction is expected to change when the wage requirement is removed.
steps.how: Request the effective month/date and whether the company needs any form or acknowledgment from you.
steps.done_when: You have a clear answer on whether your enrollment/deductions change and from which payroll.

steps.step: If you are a dependent, separately check the ¥1.30M rule
steps.action: Do not treat the ¥1.06M change as automatic permission to ignore dependent-family income rules.
steps.how: Confirm with the relevant health insurer or official guidance if your household relies on dependent coverage.
steps.done_when: You know whether the separate dependent rule still constrains your situation.

mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming 'the income wall is gone' means no social-insurance premiums.
Confusing the ¥1.06 million employee-insurance test with the separate ¥1.30 million dependent threshold.
Using annual gross income alone when the present ¥88,000 test is based on scheduled monthly wages.
Cutting work hours before checking the benefits and actual household impact.
Assuming October 1 is final without checking the official implementation date; current MHLW pages reviewed by ALAM still say October 2026 is planned.

decision_rules.if: You are already enrolled in employee social insurance
decision_rules.then: This specific abolition usually does not require a change; monitor only if HR says your classification changes.

decision_rules.if: You are a covered short-time worker scheduled at least 20 hours weekly and have been relying on the ¥88,000 wage test
decision_rules.then: Ask HR now how the October change affects enrollment and payroll.

decision_rules.if: You work under 20 scheduled hours weekly
decision_rules.then: Do not assume the wage-test abolition alone makes you eligible; verify the remaining official conditions.

decision_rules.if: Your household relies on dependent-family insurance
decision_rules.then: Check the separate dependency rules instead of relying on the '¥1.06M wall' headline.

action_plan.follow_up: Re-check MHLW or Japan Pension Service guidance when the final implementation date is formally confirmed and compare it with your employer's first affected payroll.
